## How the search stays fast

Every criterion in the package depends on the data only through a few
quantities of the least-squares fit on the selected columns $X_S$:
$$
Y^\top H Y = b^\top M b, \qquad
\mathrm{RSS} = Y^\top Y - Y^\top H Y, \qquad
b = X_S^\top Y, \quad M = (X_S^\top X_S)^{-1}.
$$
So the $n \times n$ hat matrix $H$ is never formed. The search keeps $M$ and $b$
for the current model and scores each proposed move with a rank-one update.

* **Adding** a column $x_z$: with $u = X_S^\top x_z$,
  $s = x_z^\top x_z - u^\top M u$ and $e = x_z^\top Y - b^\top M u$,
  $$Y^\top H Y \;\to\; Y^\top H Y + e\,e^\top / s .$$
* **Removing** column $j$: with $\hat\beta_j = (M b)_j$,
  $$Y^\top H Y \;\to\; Y^\top H Y - \hat\beta_j^\top \hat\beta_j / M_{jj} .$$

Scoring a move costs $O(nK + K^2)$ for a model with $K$ variables, and $M$ is
only updated when a move is accepted. Version 0.1.2 rebuilt $H$ for every
proposal, at $O(n^2 K)$ cost per move.

## Timings

Speed-up over version 0.1.2 (Julia search only, EBIC or SIC, Apple M-series
laptop). Both versions select the same variables at every step:

| $n$ | $p$ | Passes | 0.1.2 | Current | Speed-up |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1000 | 100 | 2 | 0.18 s | 0.002 s | 91× |
| 3000 | 100 | 2 | 1.29 s | 0.005 s | 247× |
| 3000 | 100 | 2 (EBIC) | 1.61 s | 0.004 s | 371× |
| 2000 | 400 | 1 | 1.74 s | 0.046 s | 38× |

Larger problems, timed from R with `GICSelection()` (EBIC, 10 true
predictors, start from 20 variables, `k = 100`, `Nsim = 3`). The time includes
copying `X` from R to Julia, and every run recovered exactly the 10 true
predictors:

| $n$ | $p$ | Time |
|--:|--:|--:|
| 500 | 1,000 | 0.9 s |
| 1,000 | 5,000 | 7.6 s |
| 2,000 | 10,000 | 26 s |

To time your own problem:

```{r}
library(GICHighDimension)
setup_julia()

set.seed(1)
n <- 1000; p <- 5000
X <- matrix(rnorm(n * p), n, p)
Y <- as.numeric(X[, 1:10] %*% rep(1, 10) + rnorm(n))

system.time(
  fit <- GICSelection(X, Y, 1:20, "Calculate_EBIC", "Calculate_EBIC_short",
                      k = 100, Nsim = 3)
)
```

The first call in a session also compiles the Julia code, which adds a few
seconds once.
